data.long_meaning: The name Graziana is derived from the Latin word 'Gratia', which means 'grace' or 'graciousness'. In Christian tradition, this name carries the spiritual significance of being a vessel of God's grace and a reflection of His divine favor. The name Graziana carries the meaning “Grace, Pleasing, Delightful” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Italian, Latin. Parents who choose Graziana usually hope their child will grow to embody grace, pleasing, delightful and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: The legend of Saint Graziana dates back to the 5th century when a young girl was martyred in the region of Lunigiana in northern Italy. She was said to have miraculously healed a blind man and, as a result, was persecuted by the Roman authorities. The story spread throughout the region, and her relics were later enshrined in a church in the town of Montemarcello.
historical_references.context: Legend of a Christian martyr in northern Italy

historical_references.reference: According to another account, Saint Graziana was a Christian princess from the ancient Roman city of Sirmium in present-day Hungary. She was martyred during the Diocletian persecution in the late 3rd century AD. Her relics were subsequently taken to Ravenna, Italy, where a basilica was built in her honor.
historical_references.context: Christian princess and martyr from Sirmium
